text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- TRADE BALANCE ACCUMULATES $937 MLN DEFICIT
Brazil posted a trade deficit of $291 million in August, bringing the deficit for this year to $937 million.
-- BNDES SAYS "CVRD IS WORTH 10 MLN REAIS"
The president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) said soon-to-be privatized state mining giant Companhia do Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) is worth 10 billion reais.
-- OPTIONS REACH 50 BLN REAIS ON BRAZIL'S FUTURES EXCHANGE

The trade in options has flourished since Brazil introduced its Real economic stabilization plan in 1994. In the first eight months of this year, 3.95 million option contracts worth 50 to 60 billion reais were traded on Brazil's futures exchange.
O GLOBO
-- GEISEL, THE ADVOCATE OF POLITICAL OPENING, DIES
Former military president Ernesto Geisel, who paved the way for Brazil's return to democracy after 21 years of military dictatorship, died of cancer yesterday age 88 in Rio de Janeiro.
-- POLICE STRIKE IN ALAGOAS STATE AND FREE PRISONERS
Civil and military police in Brazil's northeastern state of Alagoas, who have been on strike for two days, freed 30 prisoners in the state capital Maceio.
-- EXPORTS AND INVESTMENTS EXEMPT OF ICMS TAX

The Brazilian Senate approved a bill making exports of primary commodities and some semi-manufactured goods, exempt from the so-called ICMS tax. The measure also eleminates the ICMS tax on imports of capital goods and their transportation between states in Brazil.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- AMENDMENT TO ALLOCATE MORE MONEY TO PRIMARY EDUCATION
Brazil's Congress issued an amendment which stipulates that states and municipalities have to spend at least 15 percent of their revenues on primary education.
-- GOVERNMENT TO CLOSE DOWN 25 STATE COMPANIES
The Brazilian government is being advised to shut down 25 state-owned companies, which have not been named yet, to cut costs.
-- VIEIRA MIGHT GIVE UP CONTROL OF BAMERINDUS
Brazilian Senator Jose Eduardo de Andrade Vieira has hinted he might give up control of private bank Bamerindus as part of an agreement with the Central Bank to rescue Bamerindus.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
